summary: Beata Grant is a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She earned her Ph.D. from Stanford University (~1980–1987). She held a postdoctoral fellowship at UC Berkeley (~1987–1989) and became Associate Professor of Chinese Language and Literature at Washington University in St. Louis (~1989).

Beatrice Erskine Lane Suzuki was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at Radcliffe College (~1894–1898) under William James, Josiah Royce, and George Santayana, and later pursued studies at Columbia University (~1906–1909).

Ben Jiao specializes in Tibetology. He earned his Ph.D. from Case Western Reserve University (~1996–2001) under doctoral supervisor Melvyn C. Goldstein. He has served as Deputy Director of the Contemporary Tibetan Research Institute at the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences.
Ben Joffe is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. He earned his Doctor of Philosophy from the University of Colorado Boulder (~2012–2019) under the supervision of Carole McGranahan.

Benedetta Lomi specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She completed her PhD at SOAS University of London (~2012) and has held posts at the University of Virginia as a teacher and at the University of Bristol (~2017).

Benimadhab Barua was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at Chittagong College, Krishnagar Government College, Krishnath College, the University of Calcutta (~1911–1913), and the University of London (~1914–1917), later serving at the University of Calcutta (1918–1948).

Benjamin A. Elman is a scholar of Sinology and history/archaeology. After studying at Hamilton College, American University, and the University of Pennsylvania (~1974–1980), he held posts at UCLA (~1986–2002), the Institute for Advanced Study (1999), and Princeton University (~2007–2011).

Benjamin Bogin specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Michigan (~1999–2006) under Donald S. Lopez Jr., alongside committee members Luis Oscar Gómez, Tomoko Masuzawa, James Robson, and Janet Gyatso.

Benjamin Brose works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed his Ph.D. at Stanford University (~2003–2009) under supervisors Carl Bielefeldt and Bernard Faure, later serving as Assistant Professor at the University of Michigan (~2009–2016).
Benjamin I. Schwartz was a scholar in Sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at Harvard University (~1946–1950) and subsequently held an academic post there from ~1950 to 1987.

Benjamin Wood specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. He completed his Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Toronto (~2008–2014) under the supervision of Frances Garrett, with Christoph Emmrich and Ajay Rao on his committee.

Benkyo Shiio was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1901–1905). He held posts at Waseda University, Taisho University (~1926–1943), and served as head (館長) of the Sanko Library (~1948–1968).

Benoît Vermander works in Sinology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at Paris Institute of Political Studies, Yale University, Fu Jen Catholic University, and Facultés Loyola Paris. He served at Taipei Ricci Institute (1996–2009) and Fudan University (2009).

Bernard Faure works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. He studied at Paris Diderot University and the University of Paris (~1975–1984). He held posts at Cornell (~1983–1987), Stanford (~1987–2006), and Columbia University (~2006–2021).

Bernard Frank was a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who studied under Rolf Alfred Stein. He served as head of Maison Franco-Japonaise (~1972–1974) and held the chair of Civilisation japonaise at the Collège de France (1979–1996).

Bernhard Forssman was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1954–1960) and held academic posts at the University of Marburg (1968–1983) and the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (1983).

Bernhard Geiger was a scholar of Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Vienna (~1900–1904) and held posts there (~1909–1938), at the Tibetan-Iranian Institute (1938–1951), and at Columbia University (~1951–1956).
Bernhard Hirzel was an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Göttingen and under Franz Bopp (~1830–1833). He held a post as Dozent at the University of Zurich (~1833–1835).

Bernhard Kölver was an Indology scholar who held positions at the University of Cologne (1966–1970), the Nepal Research Centre (1970–1972), the University of Kiel (1977–1993), and Leipzig University (1993–2001).

Bernie Glassman was a figure in Buddhist and religious studies who founded Zen Peacemakers. He studied at New York University Tandon School of Engineering (~1956–1960) and under traditional teacher Taizan Maezumi (~1967–1995).
